standard_prerequisites.name: The halting set K
standard_prerequisites.statement: K = {x : phi_x(x) converges} is computably enumerable but not computable.
standard_prerequisites.use: K reduces to Tot; non-computability of K transfers along the reduction.

standard_prerequisites.name: s-m-n theorem
standard_prerequisites.statement: For each e there is a primitive recursive k(x) with phi_{k(x)}(y) equal to a prescribed partial computable function of (x,y).
standard_prerequisites.use: Freezes y out: k(x) indexes the function that is 0 when phi_x(x) halts and undefined otherwise.

core_obligations: Reduction construction (proof lines 2249-2277): define h(x,y) = 0 if x in K, undefined otherwise (h ignores y); h is partial computable, realised as Zero(mu s T(x,x,s));
s-m-n gives primitive recursive k(x) with phi_{k(x)} total iff x in K; so k reduces K to Tot, and computability of Tot would make K computable - contradiction.
proof_roadmap: Build the y-independent partial computable h from the halting predicate.
Apply s-m-n to obtain k(x) whose totality encodes x in K.
Conclude k is a reduction of K to Tot.
difficulty_reason: Non-computability of Tot (statement 2244-2247, proof 2249-2277): one reduction construction, both the h definition and the s-m-n freezing are carried in-span. H2.
